transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (HelioHead ML), Devon Price (SRE), Liam O'Connor (Product), Priya Menon (Security)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): OK hi everyone, thanks for making time. We wanted to keep this tight — status on staging and then benchmarks and fallback. Samira has the numbers.
[00:24] Samira (Redwood SE): Hey, yeah. Quick recap: we ran the initial run yesterday against the staging harness you gave us, Marta — thanks for the creds. We tested three variants: redwood-standard-14b, quant-14b, and a smaller 6b for fallback. The 14b median latency was about 220ms at batch size 1 for 128 tokens, p95 around 780ms. The quant path drops cost by roughly 40% but p95 widened a bit to ~950ms in some bursts.
[01:05] Marta (Helio): Just to check — those numbers are from our staging VMs in eu-west-1?
[01:09] Samira (Redwood SE): Yes, the harness was in eu-west-1 on your subnet with the test gateway. There were a couple network retries during the 2nd run that bumped p99; we noted NAT gateway egress as a possible source.
[01:27] Devon (SRE): Right, we saw some transient SNAT exhaustion on Friday evening, we added ephemeral ports but not 100% sure it's resolved. We'll confirm.
[01:35] Liam (Product): The important thing for us is stable p95 under 900ms for the user-facing flows. If you can get it consistent with caching and batching, that's good.
[01:45] Alex (Redwood): Good callout. Samira, can you talk through the cache and batching knobs you tried?
[01:50] Samira (Redwood SE): Sure. We tested automatic prefix caching for repeated system prompts which shaved about 10-15% off p50. For batching we tried continuous batching up to batch size 8 with dynamic timeouts — that lowered cost per token but increased tail latency for some single-user low-latency paths. So our suggestion is to keep latency-sensitive routes on single inference with prefix KV cache, and background or lower priority routes on batched cores.
[02:20] Marta (Helio): That matches our thinking. We have two flows: interactive triage and nightly bulk enrichment. So route separation is fine.
[02:28] Priya (Security): A couple security items — we need proof of SOC2 controls, audit log format, and how KMS keys are used for model input at rest. Are those in the security pack you already sent?
[02:40] Jordan (Redwood CSM): We shared a security bundle last week but I can re-send a version with the KMS diagrams and an end-to-end audit flow showing logs per request ID. I'll flag the page to Priya.
[02:52] Priya (Security): Also, what about private deployments? At some point we may want Redwood Private behind our VPC. Is there a matrix of differences vs hosted?
[03:00] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we have a one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem components; we'll include the matrix and the checklist for the onboarding knobs.
[03:12] Devon (SRE): For the immediate test harness, what do you need from our side to remove network flakiness? We can open holes, change NAT, etc.
[03:20] Samira (Redwood SE): Ideally: a dedicated test subnet with stable egress, service account with just-in-time creds, and confirm that the gateway isn't doing heavy packet inspection on the test path. Also, collect a tcpdump for one failing run so we can see if retries are at the app or network layer.
[03:40] Devon (SRE): We can do that. I'll provision the subnet and send the service account this week.
[03:45] Marta (Helio): Quick question about model routing — if the primary model is saturated, can we auto-fail to the 6b? What's Redwood's approach?
[03:53] Samira (Redwood SE): Yes, we support policy-based fallback. You can configure routing by latency or cost thresholds. Typical playbook: if p95 > 1s for 3 consecutive minutes, route to quant- or to the 6b for best-effort completions while we shed load. You can also do canary percentages to limit exposure.
[04:12] Alex (Redwood): Important to document expected quality delta. Marta, do you want the team to run A/B on a small eval set to measure MRR/quality drop when failing to 6b?
[04:20] Marta (Helio): Yes, please. We'll provide two canonical prompts and a small labeled set — maybe 200 examples.
[04:25] Liam (Product): We'll want the rollback playbook too — i.e., how to detect noisy outputs and force a retry on a higher-quality path.
[04:32] Samira (Redwood SE): We have an automated retry-with-fallback policy and a scoring hook you can plug in — if confidence is below threshold, we either retry on the same model or force the higher capacity. That adds latency of course but reduces bad outputs.
[04:46] Priya (Security): About KMS — are customer keys used for model weights or for storage only? We need clarity.
[04:52] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Keys are used for customer data at rest and for storing user payloads; model weights remain part of the runtime. For Private deployments we can do HSM integrations for additional control.
[05:05] Priya (Security): OK ok, send the integration diagram.
[05:10] Alex (Redwood): Switching to the benchmark sheet — Samira, curious about the p99 spikes you mentioned.
[05:14] Samira (Redwood SE): Some p99 spikes coincided with background GC activity on the test host and the SNAT exhaustion Devon mentioned. We saw one 3.2s spike. The majority of requests stayed under 1s. We recommend re-running with the newly provisioned subnet and adding an infra trace to correlate.
[05:35] Devon (SRE): We'll also swap to a managed NAT that has more ports during the test.
[05:38] Alex (Redwood): Great. On cost — we gave you estimates for tokens and the quantized model was attractive. Marta, is cost sensitivity a top priority or is latency the driver?
[05:48] Marta (Helio): It's a mix. For interactive Triage latency beats cost. For background enrichment cost matters. We'll probably want different policies per route.
[05:58] Samira (Redwood SE): We'll include a recommended config set: 'interactive' with single-shot low-latency profile, prefix cache on, no batching; 'enrichment' with batching and quantization; and 'degraded' policy for fallback routing.
[06:12] Alex (Redwood): Can you also include token accounting examples and per-1000-request cost delta so finance can eyeball it?
[06:18] Samira (Redwood SE): Yep, will add that to the sheet.
[06:22] Liam (Product): On instrumentation — can Redwood push traces into our tracing backend or do we pull?
[06:28] Jordan (Redwood CSM): We support both. We can ship trace events to your collector via OTLP or you can pull via the Console export. We'll include the config in the onboarding guide.
[06:40] Marta (Helio): One more thing — rate limiting. If we have bursty inbound traffic, what's Redwood's recommended front-door?
[06:47] Alex (Redwood): We recommend client-side smoothing and token buckets, then the Redwood API layer has per-route quotas and priority. For enterprise Dedicated you can get reserved capacity with predictable throughput.
[06:58] Priya (Security): Do you have an SLA for Dedicated? We need to know uptime and latency SLOs for contractual purposes.
[07:05] Alex (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated comes with an SLA; I can attach the SLA doc. For early POC we don't usually sign a formal SLA, but we can provide throughput targets for the pilot.
[07:15] Devon (SRE): For the re-run, what test patterns would you like us to execute? Single-user, bursty, and mixed?
[07:21] Samira (Redwood SE): Exactly. Single interactive (1 user, low tokens), bursty (100 concurrent small requests), and long-context runs (single but 8k-16k tokens) to stress KV and cache. Also one mixed pattern where some percent get routed to enrichment.
[07:38] Liam (Product): We'll also run a few end-to-end UX latencies so product can sign off.
[07:43] Alex (Redwood): Cool. I'll summarize the tech next steps.
[07:47] [--mid-call logistical pause-- someone reconnects--]
[08:05] Alex (Redwood): Back — Jordan will resend the security bundle and Samira will re-run the batch traces. Devon will provision subnet and NAT changes, Marta will deliver prompts and labelled eval.
[08:18] Marta (Helio): Sounds good. Are there any blockers from Redwood's side to do the peering and KMS test?
[08:24] Samira (Redwood SE): We just need the service account and a routing entry. We'll share the exact IAM role. No hard blockers.
[08:30] Priya (Security): Also please redact any PII from logs we send.
[08:34] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Of course, we'll provide redaction tooling pointers.
[08:40] Alex (Redwood): Let's talk fallback playbook specifics — Samira, outline the 3-step escalation.
[08:44] Samira (Redwood SE): Step 1: automatic model routing to quant-variant when p95 breaches configured threshold for > 3min. Step 2: if errors escalate or quality drops beyond X, route to 6b under canary 20% and flag for manual review. Step 3: if sustained, activate degraded mode and notify SRE/ops while traffic is rate-limited. We'll produce a YAML playbook for your ops runbook.
[09:10] Devon (SRE): Will that tie into our PagerDuty?
[09:13] Alex (Redwood): Yes we can emit alerts to your PagerDuty or forward via webhook.
[09:18] Priya (Security): We want to see the audit trail for any automated fallback decisions — who/what triggered it.
[09:24] Jordan (Redwood CSM): That's included in the trace event and the request-level audit logs we'll show you.
[09:30] Marta (Helio): OK, quick recap for our internal deadlines: we'd like the re-run and subnet by Monday and an initial security review next Thursday. Does that align?
[09:41] Alex (Redwood): Yes Monday for infra and Thursday 19th for security review.
[09:46] Alex (Redwood): Any other questions?
[09:50] Liam (Product): Nothing else. Thanks.
[09:52] Alex (Redwood): Great. We'll follow up in CRM with the sheet and the playbook draft. Thanks everyone.

Auto-generated action items (recap):
- Alex to attach benchmark CSV & onboarding checklist to CRM.
- Samira to re-run batching tests at 16k context and share traces.
- Devon to provision staging subnet and confirm NAT settings.
- Marta to share canonical prompts and the 200-example eval set.

End of transcript.
